sections.heading: EPDM Rubber Roofing on Bloomfield Homes: Benefits and Downsides

runs.v: EPDM stays flexible in the cold, and that cold-temperature flexibility and freeze-thaw resistance suit colder climates like northern New Jersey; it also resists UV exposure, ozone, and weathering, the local weather resistance and durability New Jersey roofs need. With more than 50 years of proven performance, EPDM is often described as more durable than modified bitumen and built-up roofs, is easier to maintain than older flat roofing systems, resists moss and mildew, and stays cost-effective next to other roofing options. It is also called eco-friendly, since EPDM is often described as fully recyclable at the end of its life.

black EPDM's heat retention, the reason it is preferred in colder climates, also warms a top-floor bedroom in summer, and TPO's reflective white surface can lower summer cooling costs instead. Seams depend on adhesive and tape, the membrane can shrink at the edges, and plain rubber looks utilitarian from an upstairs window; a white EPDM sheet or a reflective roof coating can improve energy efficiency, and careful attention at seams and flashing prevents most leaks.

sections.heading: EPDM Installation Methods and Roof Coatings for Flat Roofing

runs.v: are used: fully adhered EPDM is glued to the deck or an insulation layer and gives the greatest resistance to wind uplift, mechanically fastened EPDM is the quickest to install, and ballasted EPDM uses stones or pavers to hold the membrane in place, a fit for larger low-slope commercial roofs. EPDM systems can be designed for substantial wind-uplift requirements, and membranes come in widths from about 7.5 to 50 feet and thicknesses from about 30 to 100 mils, with 45 and 60 mils common, so a small Bloomfield extension or garage roof can often take one sheet with no field seam, a watertight membrane with no laps to fail.

a coating made for EPDM can restore an aged membrane that is still watertight, while a brittle, badly shrunk, or wet roof needs a full replacement, and many Bloomfield homeowners have EPDM roofing installed on a porch or extension during the main roof replacement so the flashing ties together.

faqs.q: How long does an EPDM rubber roof last on a Bloomfield home?

runs.v: EPDM rubber lasts 15 to 25 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart; other sources put EPDM roofing systems at 20 to 30 years with maintenance, and industry research puts properly maintained EPDM at about 38 years, or 40 years or more with proper installation and optimal conditions. Proper maintenance extends that life significantly, so check the laps and perimeter every year.

faqs.q: Why does an EPDM roof leak at the seams on a Bloomfield flat roof?

runs.v: The adhesive joining two membrane sheets breaks down before the rubber field degrades, per HomeGuide membrane-repair guidance, and shrinkage at the edges and penetrations is the second failure point, so Newark Quality Roofing checks the seams first, then the flashing.

faqs.q: Is EPDM or TPO better for a Bloomfield two-family or garden-apartment flat roof?

runs.v: Both are single-ply membranes: EPDM lasts 15 to 25 years and fails most often at adhered seams, while TPO lasts 7 to 20 years and fails at welded seams, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart. TPO's reflective surface can lower cooling costs and EPDM handles cold better, so Newark Quality Roofing prices both for the specific roof.

faqs.q: Can an EPDM rubber roof be repaired instead of replaced on a Bloomfield property?

runs.v: Yes, when damage stays at the laps, flashings, or edges: reseaming and adhered rubber patches fix it. Replacement follows when the membrane reaches the end of its service life or failures spread across the roof.

faqs.q: Does an EPDM roof on a Bloomfield two-family or commercial building require a permit?

runs.v: Replacing the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family home counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, with no construction permit, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. On a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months requires a permit, so confirm the scope with the Township of Bloomfield construction office; properties in a historic district can need extra review.
